extcost-add-atom-into-a-pool-with-a-decl.comment: Lowered 73.01 -> 49.01 inferences per add on 2026-08-21: space-admission-verdict reads fixed contract heads directly, has_declared_type takes an indexed ground declaration hit before its exact fallback, and petta_hook_eval skips an already-current module switch. The capacity counter's claimed-path selector makes the final row 51.01 while leaving the unclaimed write path untouched. Semantics are pinned by metta_has_declared_type, hooks_compiled_fire, hooks_admission_sugar, and the admission differential.

P12.4 first replaced per-add atom enumeration with space_atom_count/2. Direct fixed-head contract reads and the same-module compiled-fire path lowered the configured row to 87.02 inferences per add on 2026-08-21. A rollback-safe dynamic count installed only for capacity-claimed native pools lowers it again to 60.01; adds replace it atomically under its mutex and the judge reads its indexed fact instead of enumerating storage predicates.

extcost-add-atom-no-claims-on-the-space.comment: Lowered 54223 -> 34225 on 2026-08-20 with P12.4, 49.22 -> 29.01 inferences per add: petta_install_admission wrapped metta_add_atom globally, so once any pool declared a contract EVERY space's adds paid the wrapper's forall over the contract atoms. Enforcement is a per-pool hook claim now, and a space nothing claimed keeps the direct write path.

extcost-add-atom-through-an-accept-all-p.comment: Claim-time compilation first lowered this row from 234.03 to 64.02 inferences per add, and P12.4 removed the global admission wrapper. The same-module fire path lowered 44.02 -> 37.02 on 2026-08-21. The capacity counter's single claimed-path presence probe makes the final row 39.02; no unclaimed write runs that probe. Semantics are pinned by hooks_compiled_fire and the named-declarer admission test.

extcost-m-define-annotated.comment: Lowered from 75241 on 2026-08-16, -27000 over 3000 calls, which is nine inferences per call. A literal argument's type is settled while the call site compiles, so translate_args_by_type_dl/7 emits no has_type/2 check for one; a call whose arguments are all literals of the declared types now compiles to exactly what the untyped one does, with no once/1 wrapper either. The published table's annotated row moved 20.00 -> 11.00 inferences per call and 6.67x -> 3.67x against an ordinary MeTTa function. The drop is one-directional and never rejects: a literal of the WRONG declared type keeps its check and is still refused, because a get-type extension may give a literal a second type and deciding that statically would be unsound. Guarded by translator_literal_type_checks in tests/prolog/translator.plt.
